reason:
The finding stands. I read the code and did not run it in a browser. The arithmetic does not depend on a run.

Evidence:
- /Users/rufus/lumen-next/apps/web/src/pages/session/Session.tsx 148-153: the rule runs in useEffect, keyed on stepCount. It runs after React commits the new step. At that time scrollHeight includes the new block, and scrollTop still has its old value. Browser scroll anchoring does not move scrollTop when content is appended below the viewport.
- For a reader exactly at the foot, scrollHeight - scrollTop - clientHeight equals the height of what was appended. The rule follows only when that height is less than 160 px.
- /Users/rufus/lumen-next/apps/web/src/pages/session/parts.tsx 198-210: a tool step with output draws a <pre> with max-h-80 (320 px), plus py-3 padding and the header line. That is about 370 px. The step at 165-197 draws about 37 px per row, so six rows or more pass 160 px. The kernel allows 50 rows. A long 'reply' or 'thinking' paragraph has no height cap and passes 160 px too.
- No code restores the follow: no overflow-anchor rule, no useLayoutEffect, no scroll listener that records the position. Session.tsx line 223 (flex-1 overflow-y-auto) is the only scroll container. After one miss, each later step adds distance, so the follow never resumes until the reader scrolls down by hand.
- A reconnect snapshot that adds several steps at once has the same result.

Severity: should-fix. No data is lost and the reader can scroll by hand. But commit a0a2caa added the follow rule, and the rich steps of this same branch (output, rows) are the steps that defeat it. The feature fails in its main case.

Fix: decide 'was at the foot' before the append. Record the distance in an onScroll handler, or subtract the growth from the distance.

The secondary point is correct and harmless: stepCount counts the steps of every task, not only the task shown.
